text: In Strasbourg, a mysterious woman suddenly began dancing in the streets. She appeared unable to control her movements.
Within days, dozens joined her. They danced for hours, their bodies exhausted, as frightened residents watched helplessly.
Doctors blamed the summer heat and the stars. But the strange dancing continued, leaving authorities desperate for answers.
Officials eventually banned public dancing and drums. The city was struggling to control an illness nobody understood.
Later accounts claimed hundreds were affected, and some danced until they died. But historians still dispute those terrifying death reports.
Some believed they were cursed by Saint Vitus. Sufferers were taken to his shrine, hoping the mysterious affliction would end.
Was it mass psychological distress, illness, or something else? More than five hundred years later, the true cause remains unknown.
